<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
               <jats:p>In order to understand the relationship between planet multiplicity, mass, and composition, we present newly measured masses of five planets in two planetary systems: Kepler-323 and Kepler-104. We used the HIRES instrument at the W.M. Keck Observatory to collect 79 new radial velocity (RV) measurements for Kepler-323, which we combined with 48 literature RVs from TNG/HARPS-N. We also conducted a reanalysis of the Kepler-104 system, using 44 previously published RV measurements. Kepler-323 b and c have masses of <jats:inline-formula>
                     <jats:tex-math>

</jats:tex-math>
                     <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll">
                        <mml:msubsup>
                           <mml:mrow>
                              <mml:mn>2.0</mml:mn>
                           </mml:mrow>
                           <mml:mrow>
                              <mml:mo>−</mml:mo>
                              <mml:mn>1.1</mml:mn>
                           </mml:mrow>
                           <mml:mrow>
                              <mml:mo>+</mml:mo>
                              <mml:mn>1.2</mml:mn>
                           </mml:mrow>
                        </mml:msubsup>
                     </mml:math>
                     <jats:inline-graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" xlink:href="ajad2840ieqn1.gif" xlink:type="simple"/>
                  </jats:inline-formula>
                  <jats:italic>M</jats:italic>
                  <jats:sub>⊕</jats:sub> and 6.5±1.6 <jats:italic>M</jats:italic>
                  <jats:sub>⊕</jats:sub>, respectively, whereas the three Kepler-104 planets are more massive (10.0±2.8 <jats:italic>M</jats:italic>
                  <jats:sub>⊕</jats:sub>, <jats:inline-formula>
                     <jats:tex-math>

</jats:tex-math>
                     <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll">
                        <mml:msubsup>
                           <mml:mrow>
                              <mml:mn>7.1</mml:mn>
                           </mml:mrow>
                           <mml:mrow>
                              <mml:mo>−</mml:mo>
                              <mml:mn>3.5</mml:mn>
                           </mml:mrow>
                           <mml:mrow>
                              <mml:mo>+</mml:mo>
                              <mml:mn>3.8</mml:mn>
                           </mml:mrow>
                        </mml:msubsup>
                     </mml:math>
                     <jats:inline-graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" xlink:href="ajad2840ieqn2.gif" xlink:type="simple"/>
                  </jats:inline-formula>
                  <jats:italic>M</jats:italic>
                  <jats:sub>⊕</jats:sub>, and <jats:inline-formula>
                     <jats:tex-math>

</jats:tex-math>
                     <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll">
                        <mml:msubsup>
                           <mml:mrow>
                              <mml:mn>5.5</mml:mn>
                           </mml:mrow>
                           <mml:mrow>
                              <mml:mo>−</mml:mo>
                              <mml:mn>3.5</mml:mn>
                           </mml:mrow>
                           <mml:mrow>
                              <mml:mo>+</mml:mo>
                              <mml:mn>4.6</mml:mn>
                           </mml:mrow>
                        </mml:msubsup>
                     </mml:math>
                     <jats:inline-graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" xlink:href="ajad2840ieqn3.gif" xlink:type="simple"/>
                  </jats:inline-formula>
                  <jats:italic>M</jats:italic>
                  <jats:sub>⊕</jats:sub> for planets b, c, and d, respectively). The Kepler-104 planets have densities consistent with rocky cores overlaid with gaseous envelopes (<jats:inline-formula>
                     <jats:tex-math>

</jats:tex-math>
                     <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll">
                        <mml:msubsup>
                           <mml:mrow>
                              <mml:mn>4.1</mml:mn>
                           </mml:mrow>
                           <mml:mrow>
                              <mml:mo>−</mml:mo>
                              <mml:mn>1.1</mml:mn>
                           </mml:mrow>
                           <mml:mrow>
                              <mml:mo>+</mml:mo>
                              <mml:mn>1.2</mml:mn>
                           </mml:mrow>
                        </mml:msubsup>
                     </mml:math>
                     <jats:inline-graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" xlink:href="ajad2840ieqn4.gif" xlink:type="simple"/>
                  </jats:inline-formula>  g cc<jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>, <jats:inline-formula>
                     <jats:tex-math>

</jats:tex-math>
                     <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll">
                        <mml:msubsup>
                           <mml:mrow>
                              <mml:mn>2.9</mml:mn>
                           </mml:mrow>
                           <mml:mrow>
                              <mml:mo>−</mml:mo>
                              <mml:mn>1.5</mml:mn>
                           </mml:mrow>
                           <mml:mrow>
                              <mml:mo>+</mml:mo>
                              <mml:mn>1.7</mml:mn>
                           </mml:mrow>
                        </mml:msubsup>
                     </mml:math>
                     <jats:inline-graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" xlink:href="ajad2840ieqn5.gif" xlink:type="simple"/>
                  </jats:inline-formula> g cc<jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>, and <jats:inline-formula>
                     <jats:tex-math>

</jats:tex-math>
                     <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll">
                        <mml:msubsup>
                           <mml:mrow>
                              <mml:mn>1.6</mml:mn>
                           </mml:mrow>
                           <mml:mrow>
                              <mml:mo>−</mml:mo>
                              <mml:mn>1.1</mml:mn>
                           </mml:mrow>
                           <mml:mrow>
                              <mml:mo>+</mml:mo>
                              <mml:mn>1.5</mml:mn>
                           </mml:mrow>
                        </mml:msubsup>
                     </mml:math>
                     <jats:inline-graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" xlink:href="ajad2840ieqn6.gif" xlink:type="simple"/>
                  </jats:inline-formula> g cc<jats:sup>−1</jats:sup> respectively), whereas the Kepler-323 planets are consistent with having rocky compositions (<jats:inline-formula>
                     <jats:tex-math>

</jats:tex-math>
                     <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll">
                        <mml:msubsup>
                           <mml:mrow>
                              <mml:mn>4.5</mml:mn>
                           </mml:mrow>
                           <mml:mrow>
                              <mml:mo>−</mml:mo>
                              <mml:mn>2.4</mml:mn>
                           </mml:mrow>
                           <mml:mrow>
                              <mml:mo>+</mml:mo>
                              <mml:mn>2.8</mml:mn>
                           </mml:mrow>
                        </mml:msubsup>
                     </mml:math>
                     <jats:inline-graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" xlink:href="ajad2840ieqn7.gif" xlink:type="simple"/>
                  </jats:inline-formula>  g cc<jats:sup>−1</jats:sup> and <jats:inline-formula>
                     <jats:tex-math>

</jats:tex-math>
                     <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll">
                        <mml:msubsup>
                           <mml:mrow>
                              <mml:mn>9.9</mml:mn>
                           </mml:mrow>
                           <mml:mrow>
                              <mml:mo>−</mml:mo>
                              <mml:mn>2.5</mml:mn>
                           </mml:mrow>
                           <mml:mrow>
                              <mml:mo>+</mml:mo>
                              <mml:mn>2.7</mml:mn>
                           </mml:mrow>
                        </mml:msubsup>
                     </mml:math>
                     <jats:inline-graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" xlink:href="ajad2840ieqn8.gif" xlink:type="simple"/>
                  </jats:inline-formula> g cc<jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>). The Kepler-104 system has among the lowest values for gap complexity (<jats:inline-formula>
                     <jats:tex-math>

</jats:tex-math>
                     <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll">
                        <mml:mi class="MJX-tex-calligraphic" mathvariant="script">C</mml:mi>
                     </mml:math>
                     <jats:inline-graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" xlink:href="ajad2840ieqn9.gif" xlink:type="simple"/>
                  </jats:inline-formula> = 0.004) and mass partitioning (<jats:inline-formula>
                     <jats:tex-math>

</jats:tex-math>
                     <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll">
                        <mml:mi class="MJX-tex-calligraphic" mathvariant="script">Q</mml:mi>
                     </mml:math>
                     <jats:inline-graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" xlink:href="ajad2840ieqn10.gif" xlink:type="simple"/>
                  </jats:inline-formula> = 0.03); whereas, the Kepler-323 planets have a mass partitioning similar to that of the Inner Solar System (<jats:inline-formula>
                     <jats:tex-math>

</jats:tex-math>
                     <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll">
                        <mml:mi class="MJX-tex-calligraphic" mathvariant="script">Q</mml:mi>
                     </mml:math>
                     <jats:inline-graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" xlink:href="ajad2840ieqn11.gif" xlink:type="simple"/>
                  </jats:inline-formula> = 0.28 and <jats:inline-formula>
                     <jats:tex-math>

</jats:tex-math>
                     <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll">
                        <mml:mi class="MJX-tex-calligraphic" mathvariant="script">Q</mml:mi>
                     </mml:math>
                     <jats:inline-graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" xlink:href="ajad2840ieqn12.gif" xlink:type="simple"/>
                  </jats:inline-formula> = 0.24, respectively). For both exoplanet systems, the uncertainty in the mass partitioning is affected equally by (1) individual mass errors of the planets and (2) the possible existence of undetected low-mass planets, meaning that both improved mass characterization and improved sensitivity to low-mass planets in these systems would better elucidate the mass distribution among the planets.</jats:p>
title: A Tale of Two Peas in a Pod: The Kepler-323 and Kepler-104 Systems
